text: The classification and re-ageing rule rows and the rule version in force reach rwb-reporting through the rule-version read of rwb-decision on /api/recovery/decision/v1, declared and faked with no C row in the plan, and the upstream reclassification of R-UNI-22 arrives as an event of rwb-source-data whose name and topic the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog pins; the member names of the read and the name of that event are not fixed by any source and carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them.
why: The legacy story and the FSD name the rules as a dependency and never name a rule set, an owner or a channel, and the service owns no table of rules; the read is the smallest declared and faked surface that lets the app story build on Day 1, and the placeholder keeps an unidentified element visible instead of freezing a guess.
read: RWB-E8-002 Data (rule_row, DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015); FSD P9 A2.10.3.1 (BR-P9-010, VR-P9-010-1); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-22, R-UNI-38; TSD P9 T5.3; context pack P9
confirm: rwb-decision service owner, rwb-source-data service owner and the rwb-reporting contract owner
impact: If the owner names differ, only the client, the declaration and its fake change; the rows written, the record and the read are unaffected.

text: The reported classification is held in the existing STAGE, AGE_BAND and ROUTE rows of measure_snapshot, written under the definition version in force; this story adds no table, no column and no measure code, and the document_field entity of the legacy Data section is not read because documents belong to rwb-document.
why: The ownership rows of the service carry three measure tables and no classification table, and the dimension columns of measure_snapshot with LOV-MEASURE-DIM already express a stage, an age band and a route; adding a store would create a second owner of the same fact and a new pattern dependency the work package does not carry.
read: TSD P9 T3.1 (DF-RPT-041 to DF-RPT-052), T3.2 (LOV-MEASURE-DIM, ROUTE, AGE_BAND, QUEUE, STAGE, AGENT); context pack P9 ownership rows; RWB-E8-002 Data (document_field)
confirm: rwb-reporting service owner and the data steward of the measure set
impact: If a per-account store is later required, the write moves to a new table in rwb_reporting and the read is unchanged; the record element and the subscriptions stay as written.

text: The recompute runs as the classification step of the daily reporting run JOB-15 before the day's measure rows are published, and as the service's own event handler for a single account; the step name inside JOB-15 and the name of the recompute-on-version parameter are assumed, and the story adds no workflow and no Schedule because the ownership rows give the service none.
why: The legacy story and the FSD say only that the work runs unattended and that a trigger arrives, and the target architecture gives rwb-reporting one job and no workflow; naming the step and the parameter is a design choice of the service and not a business value.
read: RWB-E8-002 Meta (Priority Must, Depends on FEAT-RDF-03) and Story ('System'); FSD P9 A2.10.2 ('runs unattended'); context pack P9 (job JOB-15, workflows 0); _work/msr/context/P9.md
confirm: rwb-reporting service owner and the platform workflow owner
impact: If the step is placed in its own Schedule instead, one Schedule row and one platform dependency are added; the rows, the record and the read do not change.

text: The trace of this story is the feature FEAT-RPT-10 with the rules VR-P9-010-1, BR-P9-010 and R-UNI-22, R-UNI-38, R-UNI-39 and the non-functional requirement NFR-065, because the FSD 'Requirements served' table is empty and the legacy story names no requirement ID.
why: No requirement row exists to cite, and inventing a requirement ID would create a trace that no source can confirm; the feature and the rule IDs are the identifiers the sources do carry.
read: FSD P9 A2.10 and its empty Requirements served table; RWB-E8-002 Meta and Story; TSD P9 T8 and T7 (NFR-065)
confirm: business analyst of P9 and the traceability owner
impact: A requirement ID assigned later is added to section 18 and to the RTM without touching the story; the test case and rule links stand.

text: The case-side recompute of the segment, the route reopen and the hard-gate re-run of rules R-UNI-22 and R-UNI-37 stay with rwb-case, and rwb-reporting keeps only the reported classification and the record that names the rule version; the two services are joined by the case and rule events and by no shared table.
why: The story master and the FSD place the capability in P9, the higher-precedence Business Rules and Routing Logic places the action on the Workbench, and a reporting service can neither reopen a route nor re-run a gate; splitting the duty keeps both sources honoured and breaches no service boundary.
read: RWB-E8-002 Meta and Story; FSD P9 A2.10; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-22, R-UNI-37; TSD P9 T4; architecture slide 4
confirm: rwb-case service owner, rwb-reporting service owner and the business owner of the universal rules
impact: If the case service declines the recompute, the reporting service can only report the classification it receives and the route reopen becomes an unowned step; the gap row stays open until the owner is named.

text: Both stories of this key are delivered at status Draft (realignment v1); no BRD, FSD, TSD or PRD approval is required to build against the contract tag, and the release date 30 June 2027 is copied unchanged and marked tentative.
why: The realignment run carries no approval stop and the source documents are in review; the higher-precedence architecture, not an approval, is what the stories are built on, and no date is raised as a gap by the run rules.
read: FSD P9 v3 document control (Status In review); TSD P9 v2 document control (Status In review); RWB-E8-002 Meta (Epic E8, release 30 June 2027); Template and Rules R1 U7, U8 and R7.1
confirm: programme management office and the business analyst of P9
impact: A later approval changes the status row of the two documents only; the contract, the criteria and the test cases stand as written.
